title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator-metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid and applied no repairs. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The ceiling outcome invalidated preregistered power assumptions and made the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned 10-percentage-point effect. We report preregistered design choices, exact execution accounting, representative validator-trace excerpts from the archive, quantitative analysis, diagnostic failure-mode interpretation, and artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments (fault injection, multi-draw generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator coverage and repair value.

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps workflows with generative models offers productivity gains but raises operational risk: silent or wrong-but-plausible changes can produce outages. A widely advocated operational pattern is generate–verify–repair (GVR), where a generator (LLM) proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic validator performs mechanistic checks, and a repair module or human operator corrects detected defects. Prior work demonstrates GVR-like architectures in code and systems domains and motivates verifier insertion for safety, but standardized, preregistered measurements of validator coverage (false-positive/false-negative rates), detection latency, and predictive usefulness for end-to-end guarded success in NetOps are limited [1].

This study (AC-2026-03) was preregistered to test whether a multidimensional validator metric suite—coverage, FP-rate, FN-rate, mean detection latency, and an operational-impact proxy—explains end-to-end guarded success better than a single verifier pass rate. We used a paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics so baseline and guarded conditions start from the identical generated candidate per task; this isolates downstream validator-triggered repair as the only source of paired differences. Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered, artifact-archived confirmatory execution and exact quantitative report; (2) a compact, artifact-grounded diagnostic analysis explaining why the confirmatory test was degenerate in this run; and (3) concrete, reproducible preregistered prescriptions (fault injection, multi-sample draws, multi-validator comparison) required to obtain estimable validator metrics in future runs.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and system reports document rapid adoption of LLMs and agentic frameworks for NetOps tasks—intent-to-configuration translation, automated configuration generation, and VNF deployment—and identify failure modes (ticket noise, wrong-but-plausible outputs) that motivate verifier layers [2],[3],[4],[5]. Work on generate–verify–repair and related closed-loop architectures in software and code generation shows that mechanical verifiers can detect classifiable defects and guide repairs, but these demonstrations focus primarily on syntactic or compilation-level checks rather than full semantic intent alignment in NetOps [1]. Benchmark efforts for AIOps/NetOps reveal modest end-to-end success in many operational scenarios and motivate measurement of verification cost alongside correctness [2],[3].

Synthesis of these records indicates that verifier layers are a promising operational safeguard but that (a) deterministic validators vary in coverage and may fail to detect correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent outputs, and (b) systematic measurement protocols for validator FP/FN rates and operational impact inside GVR flows remain underdeveloped. Our preregistered paired design builds on these prior findings by operationalizing a validator-metric suite and executing a tightly controlled confirmatory test under shared_initial_candidate semantics; we explicitly treat prior demonstrations as motivational and avoid extrapolating empirical coverage beyond what the cited records support.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The study was preregistered (AC-2026-03). Key preregistered elements: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_scope = gpt-5-mini (provider bundle 'openai_responses'); task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false. The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; the primary test was an exact two-sided McNemar test with paired bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Power planning targeted detecting an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 at α = 0.05 with ≈80% power; that calculation assumed non-degenerate baseline prevalence and within-pair correlations considered in planning.

Task generator and constraints. Tasks were deterministically drawn from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, task_family = intent_configuration_repair_v1. Each task is an executable intent→configuration mapping: initial_state, expected_final_state, required_command_sequence, allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields). Tasks in the execution were labeled 'very_hard' or 'extreme' by generator difficulty. Task selection followed a deterministic index rule (challenging_workflow_stress_v1) and preregistered contamination/exclusion policies (strict SHA-256 duplicate exclusion and embedding cosine similarity > 0.95 exclusions); no exclusions occurred in this run.

Model and sampling configuration. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair) and maximum_model_calls = 400 as preregistered. Important artifact-grounded configuration: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly note that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is recorded in provider-call audit logs. The adapter's provider-call audit confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with exactly one shared initial generation per task.

Validator, scoring rules, and repair semantics. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator implements mechanistic intent-constraint checks and emits per-episode fields: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and repair artifacts if repairs occur. The preregistered binary scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) uses validator.valid as the success label for the confirmatory estimand. The pipeline allowed at most one repair call when validator.valid == false; repair calls and their outputs would be logged under repair_provider_trace_* fields.

Execution controls, exclusions, and missingness. Maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries). Primary analysis used complete-pair analysis only; sensitivity analyses treating missing guarded episodes as failures were preregistered but not invoked because completed_episode_count = 400 and failed_episode_count = 0. All raw responses, per-episode validator traces, provider-call traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle (execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The adapter completed the preregistered run in full: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200. Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. No contamination exclusions or semantic near-duplicate exclusions occurred (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).

Primary confirmatory outcome. The deterministic validator judged every sampled shared initial candidate valid and applied no repairs in any episode. Summaries from analysis/condition_summary.csv: baseline successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0), guarded successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided test p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. All numeric analysis artifacts (paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) are archived and match these values.

Representative validator-trace excerpt (artifact-grounded). A compact excerpt verbatim from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json (representative pair) illustrates validator outputs recorded for each episode (values reproduced exactly from the archive):

pair_id: pair-000004
normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
parsed_command_count: 4
required_command_count: 4
observed_touched_field_count: 3
valid: true
repair_applied: false
validator_id: deterministic_netops_validator_v5
validator_version: 5.0

For this exemplar the parsed and required counts matched, the validator emitted no violation_codes, and repair_applied = false. Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false hold for every archived episode; therefore repair-invocation and detection-latency distributions are empty for this run.

Diagnostic interpretation of the degenerate outcome. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline and guarded conditions evaluated the identical candidate per pair; thus any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair. The observed ceiling (baseline = guarded = 1.0) stems from three artifact-grounded, mutually reinforcing factors visible in the archive: (1) the synthetic deterministic task generator produced candidates satisfying the validator's mechanistic constraints for the recorded generation seeds and task payload encoding; (2) the single-sample-per-task sampling regime (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1) removed generator variability as a source of disagreements; and (3) the deterministic validator enforces structure-based checks but cannot detect certain semantic intent misalignments (correct-by-structure yet incorrect-by-intent) absent explicit external intent signals. These factors explain why no repairs were triggered and why the preregistered 10-percentage-point improvement target could not be observed.

Exploratory diagnostics. Per-validator FP/FN estimates are degenerate (no observed false positives or false negatives). Detection-latency and repair-invocation summaries are uninformative because repair_applied = false for all episodes. All per-episode validator traces and raw responses (execution/raw_results.jsonl) are archived to support reanalysis under alternative scoring decisions or injected-fault conditions. The execution bundle contains representative task manifest entries and shared-initial response files for multiple tasks (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt) allowing deterministic replay or post-hoc injection.
sections.discussion:
Statistical and inferential consequences. The preregistered paired, shared_initial_candidate design correctly isolates validator-triggered repair as the sole source of paired differences; however, that design also concentrates the risk that a single-sample ceiling will render the confirmatory test uninformative. With baseline success = 1.0 the paired estimator has zero empirical variance and hypothesis tests and CIs are degenerate; no statistical procedure can detect an improvement that cannot occur in the observed data. This is an important practical lesson for preregistered GVR evaluations: designs must ensure measurable baseline failure prevalence (via generator sampling, task selection, or fault injection) to estimate validator FP/FN and repair impact.

Operational interpretation of validator scope. The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 reliably enforces mechanistic constraints (observed in per-episode fields parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and valid flags). Nevertheless, being correct-by-structure (validator.valid = true) does not guarantee semantic intent alignment with human expectations. This limitation is intrinsic to mechanistic validators lacking external intent models, historical operator logs, or human feedback signals. Thus a validator that has high mechanical coverage may still miss semantic misalignments; complementary measurement approaches (operator-in-the-loop adjudication, semantic intent models, or post-change monitoring) are required when semantic preservation is critical.

Artifact-grounded follow-up prescriptions (preregistered arms). Based on archived artifacts and the execution adapter semantics, we propose three directly implementable, preregisterable follow-up arms that preserve the original infrastructure while producing estimable validator metrics:
  1) Fault-injection arm (preregister): deterministically replace the reference answer for a controlled fraction f of tasks with injected faults (syntactic errors, configuration-logic faults, or semantic-intent swaps). This creates measurable baseline invalidity and enables estimation of validator FP/FN and repair utility without altering generator code. The execution bundle already supports deterministic task replacement and contamination checks required for this arm.
  2) Multi-sample generation: set initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws per task (with recorded seeds). Permit the guarded pipeline to accept the first validator-approved draw or to request repair. Multiple independent samples reveal generator variability and create opportunities for the validator to reject some draws and enable repair to improve end-to-end success.
  3) Multi-validator and model diversity: add at least one alternative validator implementation and at least one additional model family. Comparing validator coverage across implementations will quantify sensitivity to validator design and improve external validity beyond the single validator and single-model family used here.
Each prescription is directly supported by the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter and the archived task manifests and can be preregistered to avoid post-hoc design changes.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate choice isolates repair effects but introduces single-sample ceiling risk; no post-hoc generator resampling occurred. Construct validity: validator.valid operationalizes mechanistic correctness but may not be a complete proxy for human-perceived intent alignment. External validity: synthetic task bank, single-model (gpt-5-mini), single deterministic validator, and controlled generator seeds limit generalization to heterogeneous production networks and alternative model/validator combinations. Conclusion validity: the degenerate outcome produced zero variance for the primary estimand, precluding inferential claims about validator benefit from this execution alone. These threats are documented in the archive and motivate the artifact-grounded follow-up arms above.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, the sampled gpt-5-mini seeds, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, every sampled initial candidate passed the validator's mechanistic checks so no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point improvement) were invalidated by the ceiling outcome. This result is reproducible from the archived artifacts. We publish exact execution and analysis artifacts to enable replication and recommend explicit fault-injection, multi-sample generation, and multi-validator preregistered arms as necessary next steps to produce estimable validator FP/FN behavior and repair value in operationally meaningful conditions.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
